page: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g is a general-purpose cloud server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor architecture is x86_64, supported by 16.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via 1 GB of network-attached storage, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no local GPUs bundled with this instance.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance alongside average multi-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier status in single-core stress-ng CPU tests and single-threaded compression tasks, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 25% tier, and multi-core stress-ng performance sits in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests show average read and write speeds, with cached small-block reads reaching 439.02 GB/sec and uncached large-block writes at 41.08 GB/sec.

This hardware configuration is suitable for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, redis key-value operations, and database transactions, all of which register average performance tiers. It can also handle lightweight machine learning tasks, such as small-model LLM text generation, though prompt processing for medium-sized models is poor. Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced resource distribution, the server offers a reliable resource density for standard application hosting, though workloads heavily reliant on multi-threaded decompression or local high-speed storage may face bottlenecks.
